plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n * value = 2/3 * value. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $24, so optimal bid ≈ $16, shading down to preserve profit while remaining competitive against Betty and Charles's similarly shaded bids.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to approximately (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3 bidders. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin if I win. My value is $16, so I'll bid around $10.7 to maximize expected profit while still having a reasonable chance to win against the other two bidders.

With three bidders and values uniformly distributed on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to bid a fraction (n-1)/n = 2/3 of my value, assuming others bid similarly rationally. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $24, so I'll bid approximately $16, which should give a good expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning.
